JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 02.11.2022, the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EB-9292 from Nitturu towards Tumkur with her son.

At about 1.30 p.m, when they reached near Neha Tea House, Gubbi Junction, NH-206 road,
Tumkur Town, Tumkur District, the rider of the said motorcycle drove it in a rash & negligent manner and at that time an auto driver suddenly applied the brake and due to that, the rider of the bike also applied break, but he lost control, resulting which the rider the pillion rider fell down on the road.
Due to the terrific impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It is further urged that the petitioner was shifted to M.C.Orthopedic Hospital, Tumkur wherein she was treated as inpatient.
During the course of treatment she underwent several examinations and also undergone surgery and discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest and regular followup treatment.
She spent substantial amount towards her treatment.
Further at the time of accident she was working as Mason and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries she became disabled and lost her earning capacity.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
The respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.1 and 3 are insurer of the motorcycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. After service of notice, respondent No.1/Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.

This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance policy No.421700/31/2019/25815 in respect of offending vehicle in its engine and chasis number in the name of respondent No.2 and the said policy is valid from 01.12.2018 to 30.11.2023.
The package policy period only from 01.12.2018 to 30.11.2019, after expire of 30.11.2019 the insured has not renewed the said package policy and it is liability only policy.
Further it is contended that the petitioner was traveling as a pillion rider and the police have filed charge sheet against the rider of Activa scooter.
As per terms and conditions of the liability policy, risk of the pillion rider is not covered.
It is only covered risk is a third parties.
The petitioner is not a third party and the petitioner does not come within purview of M.V.Act.

Hence claim petition is liable to be Shashikala vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54331407/
2 dismissed against this respondent.

sentences.text: However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Further it is contended that the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on a motorcycle without wearing helmet hence she was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 denied the negligence on his part but contended that the unfortunate accident occurred due to suddenly apply of auto which was proceeding in front of his motor bike.
The respondent No.2 admitted that he is the RC owner of the motor bike bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EB-9292 and was duly insured with the 1st respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is further urged that in case if court comes to conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for any compensation same is to be fastened on the 1st Respondent - insurance company.

This respondent contended that in a policy motorized two wheelers (5 years)
Bundled policy with policy wordings clearly mentioned that Section - II of policy it is a liability policy and the petitioner was a pillion rider as per policy terms and conditions of policy.

As per the policy, it has issued Third Party Coverage, this section generally refers to "third party" liability,
meaning anyone not directly involved in the insurance contract (like the driver or vehicle owner)
who is injured due to the vehicle's operation.
In this case also the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider and he was injured meaning thereby he was not directly involved in the insurance contract.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. After service of notice, respondent No.3/Chola MS Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

This respondent contended that based on particular furnished in the claim petition and after verification of the said policy it is learnt that the said policy is cover to risk of Third Party are fictitious.

It is further contended that this respondent had issued only Chola Standalone OWN Damage (OD) Policy for two wheeler insurance policy in favour of 2nd respondent in respect of motorcycle No.KA-50-EB-9292 and this policy is covers only for own damage of the vehicle under the policy.
No other liability in connection with the vehicle including third party liability for personal injury / property damage.
Hence the risk of the petitioner under the alleged policy is not covered and hence, there is no obligation or liability against this respondent to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

Further it is contended that this respondent does not admit that the alleged motorcycle was insured with this respondent at the alleged time and accident or this respondent has not issued any policy to cover the risk of third party under the motor policy.

This respondent has not collected / received or the owner of vehicle / respondent No.2 has not paid any premium to cover the risk of third party under the Shashikala vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54331407/
3 motor policy, hence this respondent is not liable to indemnify him.

sentences.text: Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES

1 ) Whether the petitioner proves that she met with a Road Traffic Accident on 02.11.2022 at about 1.30 p.m, near Neha Tea House, Gubbi Junction, NH-206 road,
Tumkur Town, Tumkur District and sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EB-9292 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, from whom and to what extent ?
3) What order or award ?
7. The petitioner examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 20 were marked on her behalf.
Dr.Ramachandra, Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.2.
Ex's .P21 & 22 were marked through him.
In order to prove its defence, the respondent No.3 insurance company examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.

Further the respondent No.1/Oriental insurance company examined its officer as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.3 & 4 documents.
8.
Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondents counsel on merits.
The counsel for petitioner filed written arguments.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.15 lakhs together.
The petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 being police documents.

On careful perusal of these documents it appears that based on the information given by petitioner herself the jurisdictional Police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 and investigated the matter and submitted the charge sheet as per Ex.P.9.
In order to prove the factum of negligence the petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.3, 4 being the spot mahazar and Spot Sketch and Ex.P.9 charge sheet.
On conspectus reading of Ex.P.3 & 4 it reflects that the accident happened near Neha Tea House, Gubbi Junction, NH- 206 road, Tumkur Town, Tumkur District.

On close perusal of the same it reflects that the rider of the motorcycle in which the petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider, while so proceeding in front of the motorcyel one auto was proceeding and the said Auto rickshaw driver suddenly applied the break and in order to avoid the collision, the rider of the motorcycle also appllied the break, resulting which he lost control over the motorcycle and turned turtle fell on the road and caused the accident.

If the driver of Auto and rider of the motorcycle was Shashikala vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54331407/
4 coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the rider of the motorcycle for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.9 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle.

10. Though the respondent No.1 contended that the insured vehicle is not at all involved in the accident but in order to substantiate the same absolutely no materials placed on record by respondent No.1.
Mere self serving and self proclaimed statement is not trump card for success of the case of respondent No.1.

Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P.9 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this Court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle.
In this case the rider cum owner of the motorcycle appeared and filed his written statement he impliedly admitting the involvement of the vehicle and negligent act.
Though PW.1 cross-examined at length by the respondents but she withstood the rigor of cross-examination.
This Court is aware of the fact the charge sheet cannot be trusted as a holy document to come to the conclusion of the negligence.

But in the instant case having regard to the other materials placed on record and other surrounding circumstances it is clearly forthcoming that the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle.
Therefore she is entitled for compensation.
12. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited her Aadhar card at Ex.P16,
wherein her date of birth is reflected as 01.01.1958.
This indicates that she was aged (64 years 10 months 1 days) 65 years on the date of accident.
13. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident she was working as coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in her evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.

The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the Shashikala vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54331407/
5 accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the Shashikala vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, Rs.15,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

14. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : 1)Pain, swelling right arm, 2) tender right arm, 3) Both shoulder under ROM, 4) abnormal mobility and 5) right humerus fracture.
It is needless to say that the injuries No.1 to 4 are simple and injury No.5 is grievous in nature.

The discharge summary of M.C.Orthopedic Hospital, Tumkur (Ex.P.12) indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 02.11.2022 to 04.11.2022 (3 days in total).

During the course of treatment she had undergone surgeries in the form of : MIPPO of fracture shaft of right humerus with LCP and TENS on 04.11.2022.
15.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries she has become disabled and has thereby lost her earning capacity.

Therefore she got examined Dr.Ramachandra. S as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent residual physical disability of 39.51% to the right upper limb and 13.51%
disability to the whole body.

It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and stated that he has seen only wound certificate and discharge summary and has not seen the case sheet.
He stated that fracture was united with implants in situ.
He further admitted that there is no fracture in right shoulder joint and right elbow joint.
Further there was no loss of muscles but there was weakness, there was no problem of blood circulation right shoulder joint and right elbow joint.
Generally in old age there is weakness in muscle but not in all persons.
He admitted that he has not assessed functional disability.
When such is the case physical disability assessed by the medical expert is on the higher side.

Be that as it may,
the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 7%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 7%.
16.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 3 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.3,600/- (1,200 X 3) is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: 17. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for at least 4 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.62,000/- (15,500 X 4) under this head.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P14, the petitioner has spent Rs.63,238/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.63,238/- which is rounded off to Rs.63,300/- towards medical expenses.
20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '7'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.91,140/- (Rs.15,500 X 12 X 7 X 7/100) which is rounded off to Rs.91,100/- is awarded under this head.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.10,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

23. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 3,600-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 62,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 63,300-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 91,100-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : 10,000-00 Total 3,30,000-00 24.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: Admittedly in the case on hand the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on the offending motorcycle.
From the evidence affidavit of RW.1 and Ex.R.4, it is evident that the insurance policy is a 'liability only policy', under which the risk of pillion-rider is not covered.
Further there is no proof of payment of additional premium covering the risk of other persons apart from the third parties.

In this view of the matter the respondent No.1 has relied on the decision of Honble Apex Court in (2008) 7 SCC 428 between Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Sudhakaran K.V. and others, wherein it is held that :
"25.

entities.text: Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Sudhakaran K.V. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The law which emerges from the said decisions, is : (i) the liability of the insurance company in a case of this nature is not extended to a pillion rider of the motor vehicle unless the requisite amount of premium is paid for covering his / her risk ; (ii) The legal obligation arising under section 147 of the Act cannot be extended to an injury or death of the owner of vehicle or the pillion - rider ; (iii) the pillion -rider in a two wheeler was not to be treated as a third party when the accident has taken place owing to rash and negligent riding of the scooter and not on the part of the driver of another vehicle"
26.

Further the respondent No.2 has also relying upon the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2013) 1 SCC 731 between National Insurance Company Ltd., v Balakrishnan and (2018) 15 SCC 189 between Jagtar Singh @ Jagdev Singh v Sanjeev Kumar and others, since the insurance policy was a 'Liability only policy' and not 'Comprehensive package policy', the insurer is not liable for the injuries sustained by the pillion rider of the offending motorcycle.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., v Balakrishnan and (2018) 15 SCC 189
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Jagtar Singh @ Jagdev Singh v Sanjeev Kumar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly the petition deserves to be dismissed against the respondent No.1 who is the insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50- EB-9292.
27.

The respondent No.3 has issued own Damage policy who is also insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-EB-9292 and it has issued only OD (Own damage policy in favour of respondent No.2 / owner of the vehicle.

Further the issuance of respondent No.3 policy is only for covers own damage of the vehicle and no other liability in connection with the vehicle including third party liability for personal injury / property injury.
Therefore respondent No.3 is also not liable to pay any compensation.

Thus the respondent No.2 being the owner of said motorcycle is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
28. ISSUE NO.3

: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,30,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:

Mere self serving and self proclaimed statement is not trump card for success of the case of respondent No.1.
Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P.9 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this Court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the insured vehicle.
In this case the rider cum owner of the motorcycle appeared and filed his written statement he impliedly admitting the involvement of the vehicle and negligent act.

Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
